title: Purpose Code for International Payments: Meaning, Codes and When You Need One
summary: Find the right RBI purpose code for inward or outward remittances. See P1006, P1009, P1099 and S0902 examples, plus the 2026 export rules.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


### Key Takeaways


- A purpose code is a five-character label (one letter, four digits) that states the reason for a cross-border transaction. P codes cover money coming into India; S codes cover money going out.
- You declare the purpose code for your transaction; your Authorised Dealer bank reports it to the RBI through FETERS, so correcting a wrong code means asking your bank to amend it.
- Choose the code for the transaction described in the invoice, rather than your company’s general line of business. The same client can pay you under two different codes on two different jobs.
- From 1 October 2026, a unified export and import regime replaced the 2015 rules, bringing goods, software and services under a common Export Declaration Form framework.
- Cashfree Payments holds the RBI’s Payment Aggregator Cross Border licence and publishes its supported purpose code reference for Global Collections.


Since October 1, 2026, several rules around purpose codes and export declarations have changed.


The RBI’s[new unified export and import framework](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=62049) brings software and services into a single declaration form. Software and service exporters now need to follow the applicable EDF (Export Declaration Form) process, which many did not have to complete earlier.


That said, while international payments aren’t new to Indian businesses, understanding how to use the right purpose code is still important to avoid documentation mismatches, correction requests and settlement delays.


But before we get into understanding and picking the right codes, let’s discuss when exactly you even need these codes.


##


When Do You Need a Purpose Code for International Payments?


You need it when you’re either receiving or making an international payment, but both of them create very different obligations.


### Purpose Code for Inward Remittance (P Codes)


Here, the purpose code for inward remittance determines what your Foreign Inward Remittance Advice, Statement or Certificate says, and that document is proof of the foreign receipt behind your export. Businesses comparing collection methods can also review[how to receive international business payments in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-receive-international-business-payments-in-india/) .


This remittance record can support an electronic Bank Realisation Certificate (eBRC). The Authorised Dealer bank uses the export and receipt details to update or close the relevant entry in the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS).


### Purpose Code for Outward Remittance (S Codes)


This is basically about declaration and tax.


Outward remittances may require an A2 form declaration, KYC documents, and supporting invoices or agreements that match the stated purpose. The code can affect how the remittance is reviewed for tax and compliance.[This guide explains the wider outward remittance process](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/outward-remittance-meaning/) .


Hence, it’s important that you confirm it with your bank before you initiate a large payment.


***Also read:[International Payment Terms: A Guide for Indian Exporters](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/international-payment-terms/)***


##


What Is a Purpose Code and How Do You Choose the Right One?


A purpose code is a five-character alphanumeric tag, one letter followed by four digits, that classifies why your money has crossed India’s border. The letter tells you the direction of travel.


- **P codes apply to receipts:** Money arriving in India from abroad, whether that is an export payment, a consultancy fee, or foreign investment.
- **S codes apply to payments made:** Money leaving India, for instance, when you clear a supplier invoice, pay a licensing fee, or fund an overseas office.


The first two digits tell you the group you’re sending or receiving money into, and the last two will tell you the position within that group. Put together, the code reads left to right. For instance:


**Code** **Reads as**


P0103 A receipt (P) in group 01, exports of goods: advance received against an export contract for goods


S0902 A payment (S) in group 09, charges for use of intellectual property: a licence to use a produced original or prototype, such as a manuscript or film


P0006 A receipt (P) in group 00, capital account: foreign direct investment in equity


While you don’t need to understand the mechanism of writing these codes, as the RBI defines them as a fixed set, you do need to scan the[supported purpose code list for Global Collections](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/payments/latest/international-payments/global-collections/purpose-codes) or your bank’s current list, pick the right one that matches your exact transaction, and declare it in your form.


Once that’s done, your Authorised Dealer bank uses the purpose code you provided when reporting the remittance through the applicable RBI systems. The RBI uses this reporting to compile India’s balance of payments.


If you enter the wrong code, it can affect the report your bank files and the documents produced later, including your FIRC, FIRS or FIRA and the entry your export should close against. The mismatch may require clarification or an amendment from the reporting bank.


***Also Read:[Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC): Meaning and Process](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/firc/)***


##


Common RBI Purpose Codes: P1099, P0802, S0902 and More


You’ll see dozens of purpose codes in practice. The inward and outward purpose code lists below show selected examples, not every RBI code. Match the description to your invoice and confirm the applicable code with your Authorised Dealer bank. Depending on the transaction, businesses may also need an[Import Export Code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-import-export-code-iec/) and supporting export documentation.


### Purpose Code List for Inward Remittance (P Codes)


Code Use it for


P0802 Software consultancy or implementation outside the older SOFTEX classification


P0807 Export of software covered under SOFTEX (advance payment), as described in legacy code lists


P1020 Wholesale and retail trade services


P1002 Trade-related services, commission on exports or imports


P1006 Business and management consultancy and public relations services


P1009 Architectural services


P1099 Other services not included elsewhere, for export of services


P1017 Publishing and printing services


P1019 Commission agent services


**P1006 or P1009?** A fee for management consulting or public relations may fall under P1006; a fee for architectural services may fall under P1009. Cashfree’s supported-code list separates engineering services under P1014, so check the current classification with your bank if the work combines design and engineering.


**When does P1099 apply?** Use P1099 only when the export is a service and no more specific service code fits the invoice. It is not a general code for every overseas client payment. If the work is software consultancy, advertising or another named category, check that category first with your bank.


The 2026 framework changes the declaration process for software exports. Some published code descriptions may still contain older SOFTEX wording, so confirm how your bank applies those codes under the current EDF process.


### Purpose Code List for Outward Remittance (S Codes)


Code Use it when


S0101 Making an advance payment to a foreign supplier for goods (excluding Nepal and Bhutan)


S0102 Settling an invoice for imported goods (excluding Nepal and Bhutan)


S0802 Paying an overseas vendor for software consultancy or implementation


S0901 Paying for franchise rights, patents, trademarks or industrial processes


S0902 Paying for the licensed use of a produced original or prototype, such as a manuscript or film


S1006 Paying an overseas business or management consultancy or public relations firm


Purpose codes are only one part of cross-border compliance.[This guide to GST on international transactions](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-on-international-transactions/) explains how export and import treatment can differ.

##


Keep Purpose Codes and Export Records Aligned


The purpose code affects how your export receipt is classified and matched with supporting documents. If you export services, the 2026 framework also introduces declaration requirements that may be new to your business. So do two things this month.


First, check that the code list your team works from is current, since older versions and legacy descriptions remain available online. Then start picking codes as per your invoice. Businesses setting up a broader export workflow can also use[this export-import business guide](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/export-import-business-in-india/) as a starting checklist.


Both can take an afternoon, but may save time later if a payment is held for clarification.

##


FAQs About Purpose Codes


#### What is the P0103 purpose code used for?


P0103 covers advance receipts against export contracts for goods, meaning your overseas buyer pays you before the shipment leaves India. It sits in the exports of goods group and signals to your bank that the money is a pre-shipment advance. The advance creates an obligation, because the export has to follow within the period your bank confirms.


#### What is the P0802 purpose code used for?


The P0802 purpose code generally covers receipts for software consultancy or implementation outside the older SOFTEX classification. Since the 2026 framework changed the declaration process for software exports, confirm the current code and EDF treatment with your Authorised Dealer bank.


#### What is the P1099 purpose code?


P1099 covers receipts for exported services not included in a more specific service category. Match it to the service on the invoice, not simply to the fact that the payer is overseas. Check named alternatives such as P0802 for software consultancy before confirming P1099 with your bank.


#### What is the purpose code P0006 used for?


P0006 covers foreign direct investment into India in equity, which is money an overseas investor puts into an Indian company by buying shares. It is a capital account code handled by your AD bank under FDI reporting rather than an export receipt. You will not find it on a collections platform’s purpose code list, because those lists cover trade and services receipts.


#### What is the purpose code S0902 used for?


S0902 is an outward payment code for licensed use of produced originals or prototypes, such as manuscripts and films. It sits in the intellectual property charges group. Patents, trademarks, franchises and industrial processes appear under S0901 in the RBI’s published classification; confirm the current code with your Authorised Dealer bank before paying.


#### How do I know which purpose code applies to my payment?


Start with direction. Money coming in takes a P code; money going out takes an S code. Then read the invoice line to see what that specific transaction paid for, match it against a current RBI list, and confirm the selection with your AD bank before the payment moves.


#### What is the RBI purpose code list and where is the official version?


The RBI purpose code list classifies cross-border transaction types for FETERS reporting and balance of payments compilation. Inward remittances use P codes; outward remittances use S codes. RBI reporting materials and bank lists are available in different versions, including older or withdrawn copies. Confirm the current classification with your Authorised Dealer bank; Cashfree’s linked reference above covers supported Global Collections receipts, not every inward or outward code.


#### Can a purpose code be changed after the money has landed?


Yes. Your AD bank can amend a reported purpose code on request, supported by the invoice or contract that establishes the correct one. Timelines and internal processes vary by bank, so raise it as soon as you spot the mismatch.


#### What is the difference between P codes and S codes?


P codes classify inward remittances, meaning any money arriving in India from abroad. S codes classify outward remittances, meaning money you send out of India. The same underlying activity has both, so a software consultancy fee you receive is P0802 and one you pay is S0802.


#### P0103, P0102 or P0101: which one applies?


How and when the export bill is handled decides this, not the type of goods. P0103 applies when the buyer pays before shipment, P0102 when an export bill sent on collection is realised, and P0101 when your bank negotiates, purchases or discounts the bill after shipment. Select the code that reflects the actual receipt and your bank’s handling of the export bill.


#### What changes for purpose codes and export reporting on 1 October 2026?


The 2026 Regulations replace the 2015 Export Regulations with a unified export and import regime. A single Export Declaration Form covers goods, services and software, and service exporters generally file an EDF within 30 days from the end of the relevant invoice month. For non-software services, the RBI also allows filing on or before receipt of payment. The framework also revises export-realisation timelines and reporting. Confirm the process for your transaction with your Authorised Dealer bank.


#### Which purpose code applies to a freelancer or agency invoicing an overseas client?


It depends on the service delivered rather than your job title. Software consultancy or implementation work typically falls under P0802, business and management consultancy under P1006, and advertising or trade fair services under P1007. Where the service fits none of the listed categories, P1099 is the catch-all on the current list.


#### Which purpose code applies to a SaaS business collecting subscription revenue from abroad?


Match the code to the nature of the software service being billed rather than the billing frequency. Software consultancy and implementation receipts may fall under P0802, but the classification depends on the service and current declaration process.[This guide to accepting global SaaS payments](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/indian-saas-global-payments-guide/) covers the wider payment workflow. Confirm the code with your AD bank, since SaaS billing models vary in how they are treated.


#### How do I get a FIRA, FIRS or FIRC, and what is it used for?


Your AD bank or collections provider issues the applicable document after the foreign payment is credited and the required transaction details are available. It provides evidence of the foreign receipt and can support reconciliation, audit records and eligible export-related claims. Ask the provider which document it issues and when it becomes available for your payment route.


#### How does the purpose code affect tax on export of services?


The code helps align the remittance record with the service described on your invoice. It does not by itself determine whether a supply qualifies as an export or receives a particular GST treatment. A code that contradicts your invoice weakens the supporting documentation, so confirm the treatment for your specific case with a qualified tax advise
